transcript.text: f/f freezer keeps icing up bottom drawer wont shut proper, defrosted it 2wks ago already full of ice again. indesit

This points strongly to an automatic defrost system fault rather than just user error. The most common causes are a failed defrost heater, a stuck defrost thermostat (thermal fuse), or a blocked drain letting water freeze in the wrong place. To distinguish between these, we need to look inside the freezer. Please perform a full manual defrost: switch the appliance off at the wall socket, remove all food into cool bags, lay towels down, and leave both doors open until every bit of ice has melted completely (this may take 24–48 hours). 1. Remove the rear panel inside the freezer compartment.
2. Look at the evaporator coils (the metal fins or tubes).
3. Tell me: are they covered in a solid block of ice, or are they fairly clear? This will tell us if the heater isn't melting the frost (solid ice) or if water is simply draining into the drawer area and freezing there (clear coils but wet/damp base).
its a manual defrost freezer tho, no auto defrost i dont think. ive already defrosted it 2wks ago and its iced up again that fast. what else could it be?

If it's a manual defrost model, the rapid icing is usually caused by one of two things: either warm air is getting in (bad seal) or meltwater from normal condensation isn't draining away properly (blocked drain). Because the ice is specifically preventing the bottom drawer from shutting, it sounds like water is pooling at the base and freezing there. In many Indesit models, this happens when the small drain hole at the back of the compartment gets clogged with food debris or ice. Please perform a full manual defrost again (unplug, empty, leave doors open for 24-48 hours). Once it is completely dry, please check:
1. The drain hole: Is there a small hole at the bottom rear of the compartment? Is it blocked?
2. The door seal: Does the rubber gasket look torn or loose, or just dirty? Let me know what you find with those two checks.
seal check: bottom corner of the freezer door seal is split about 5cm and the hinge-side bottom bit is flattened. not sure about a drain hole, haven't seen one. seal looks like the culprit tbh?

[Heading: Likely cause: door seal]
That split and flattened section in the bottom corner is probably the cause. A gap like that lets warm, moist air from your kitchen get into the freezer every time the door closes. Replacing the seal is a straightforward fix. To make sure you get the correct part for your specific Indesit model, I need the model number. It’s usually on a sticker inside the fridge compartment or on the door frame. Do you have that to hand?
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
model is IB55532W, indesit. read it off the rating plate. what do i search for to get the seal and is it push in or screwed? can fit it myself

[Heading: Likely cause: door seal]
Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. That split and flattened section is probably the cause of your icing. Warm kitchen air gets in through that gap, turns to moisture, and freezes rapidly at the bottom where it can't escape. 1. What to search for: Go to a reputable spare parts website (such as Indesit's own site, PartMaster, or Appliance Parts Direct) and search for "Indesit IB55532W door seal" or "gasket". 2. Is it push-in or screwed? Most modern fridge-freezer seals are held in by a plastic retaining strip that clips into a groove around the inside of the door frame. You usually have to pull out the old strip (often with a screwdriver) and clip the new one in. Some older models use screws, but the clip-in style is far more common for Indesit.
3. Can you fit it yourself? Yes, this is a standard DIY job. It involves no electricity or water connections. You simply remove the old seal/strip and press/clip the new one into place. It can be fiddly to get the corners right, but it requires no special tools other than perhaps a flat-head screwdriver. Once you have the part fitted, run the freezer for 24 hours to see if the icing stops. If the ice returns quickly even with a good seal, we would then look at internal drainage issues.
